highlights.title: Microsoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concerns
highlights.description: Microsoft is publishing a 37-page "humanist AI code of conduct" today, amid growing safety concerns over AI model progress. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a coordinated slow down of AI development over the weekend, after researchers warned recently that AI model progress could outpace our ability to safely deploy increasingly complex systems and verify and control the actions of AI agents. Microsoft's AI code of conduct makes it clear that "people matter more than AI," and that AI models

highlights.title: OpenAI boss Sam Altman spells out how and why the AI industry wants to slow down: 'We could lose control'
highlights.description: OpenAI's chief has made comments detailing how AI safety frameworks and a slowdown could work, as the industry unites behind concerns.

highlights.title: AI Bosses Risk Clash With Wall Street and Trump Over Safety
highlights.description: Anthropic PBC and OpenAI will have to weigh their calls to tap the brakes on artificial intelligence development against forces in the tech industry, financial markets and the Trump administration that are likely to resist any substantial slowdown.

highlights.title: AI stocks slide after major CEOs unite to urge slowdown
highlights.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said the industry "must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," amid growing concerns over risks from AI.

highlights.title: Anthropic's Solution to AI Danger Is 'Quite Vague': Opinion
highlights.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson discusses Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei's proposal that AI labs should slow down their most cutting-edge research. "Pacing or slowing down does also just essentially kick the can down the road," Olson says on Bloomberg Television. "Dario's essay was quite vague in terms of how he thinks that should happen." (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: OpenAI’s Altman Voices Support for ‘Pacing’ AI Development
highlights.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman on Sunday added his support to the idea of “pacing” AI development, so that cutting-edge models don’t outrun the ability of humans to maintain control.

highlights.title: Apple's Siri AI Can Be Swapped Out for Claude, ChatGPT, Code Shows
highlights.description: Code sleuth "pdfu" has uncovered iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate private frameworks that show Apple has designed its new Siri architecture to work with third-party AI models at what appears to be a surprisingly deep level. One mechanism called Model Delegation allows Claude to appear as a Siri extension in the same way as the existing built-in ChatGPT extension. In pdf's video, shared on X, the macOS user brings up the "Search or Ask" bar and chooses Claude as the AI model via an "Ask..." contextua

highlights.title: China Rejects AI 'Fearmongering' as CEO's Urge Slowdown
highlights.description: China criticized dire warnings about AI's risks after leading US technology executives backed calls to slow the development of advanced models and warned that a Chinese advantage could threaten American national security. spokesman Guo Jiakun said "Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance and serve the interests of no one,". highlights.title: TikTok developer ByteDance arranges $29.6 billion loan as it builds AI ambitions
highlights.description: ByteDance was reportedly considering spending $70 billion on AI data centers and infrastructure. The news comes as U.S. AI giants call for slowing the AI race.

highlights.title: OpenAI President on Doing Business in the Wake of Hugging Face

ai.description: Cybersecurity concerns are feeding a broader AI safety debate, with industry leaders calling for measures to slow frontier AI development.

business.title: Ligent Technologies Seeks $727 Million in Hong Kong IPO
business.description: AI computing networks maker Ligent Technologies Inc. is seeking to raise as much as HK$5.7 billion ($727 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, adding to a surge of listings this year tied to the global artificial intelligence buildout.

business.title: Fintech Tabby Hits Valuation of $6.5 Billion, Topping Klarna
business.description: Gulf fintech firm Tabby said it was valued at $6.5 billion in an investment round led by Blue Pool Capital, the Hong Kong investment firm that manages the assets of Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s Chairman Joseph Tsai.

business.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Demand Crashes Some Local Trading Apps
business.description: Demand for the continent’s biggest initial public offering, the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, overwhelmed some of the many Nigerian investing apps soon after the share sales started.

business.title: RBC’s Calvasina Wraps ‘AI Froth’ Into Earnings Risks
business.description: Lori Calvasina, head of US equity strategies at RBC, discusses earnings risks for stocks from the artificial intelligence buildout and what her firm sees on technology capex outside of the top 10 markets cap names in the S&P 500. (Source: Bloomberg)

business.title: M&G's Municchi Says Investors 'More Wary' About AI Trade
business.description: Maria Municchi, multi asset fund manager at M&G Investments, discusses the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade after leaders of the biggest firms proposed slowing the technology’s development. She tells Bloomberg Television that while "price will continue to behave pretty well," markets are becoming "a little bit more wary" about whether the capex boom will translate into delivered earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

business.title: China says AI CEOs' call for a slowdown is 'fear mongering'
business.description: Chinese state media's reports of the daily press conference also noted that all groups should work together for AI openness and inclusivity.

chips_cloud.title: Intel-Backed Construction AI Firm Buildots Raises $130 Million
chips_cloud.description: Buildots, a startup that uses artificial intelligence to help speed up construction of expensive mega-projects like data centers, chip factories and hospitals, has raised $130 million in new financing.

chips_cloud.title: Data Center Firm Firmus Said to Seek $5 Billion in Australia IPO
chips_cloud.description: Firmus Technologies Pty is looking to raise as much as $5 billion in an initial public offering in Australia, according to people familiar with the matter.

chips_cloud.title: Modders halve FSR 4 render times on AMD’s PS5-derived BC-250 mining APU — portable FidelityFX DLL cuts 1440p upscaling time from 11.51 ms to 5.92 ms
chips_cloud.description: Modders have nearly halved FSR 4 processing time on AMD’s PS5-derived BC-250, using a portable FidelityFX DLL that cuts 1440p upscaling cost to 5.92 ms.

other.title: ICBC, HSBC Among Major Lenders on $30 Billion ByteDance Loan
other.description: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has signed a $29.6 billion loan with more than two dozens lenders, including Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Ltd. and HSBC Holdings Plc, in one of Asia’s biggest dollar-denominated deals this year.

other.title: Huawei pitches near-packaged optics as co-packaged costs bite
other.description: 7.2 Tbps module arrives ahead of standards, with promises of fewer repair headaches

other.title: Meta Quest user vibe-codes 3D object throwing to 3D printer — ‘I've never felt more like Tony Stark’ says the software engineer
other.description: A software engineer has shown off a futuristic Meta Quest plus 3D printer workflow where models are 'thrown' to the output device.

other.title: Ed Conway on the Fragile World of Global Trade
other.description: Merryn Somerset Webb talks with Ed Conway, economics and data editor at Sky News and author of "Trade World," about the vast and often invisible supply chains behind the things we buy and whether decades of globalization have made economies more resilient or dangerously dependent. They also discuss China’s manufacturing advantage, and whether the UK and Europe can rebuild their industrial base without giving up the cheap goods consumers have come to expect. (Source: Bloomberg)

other.title: Is AppleCare really worth the extra cost?
other.description: AppleCare provides peace of mind against damaged devices, but it's an additional cost you have to weigh.

other.title: Best Noise-Canceling Earbuds (2026): Bose, Apple, Samsung, Beats, and More
other.description: I’ve tested dozens of wireless earbuds. These are the best for when you want to tune out the world, wherever you are.

devices.title: Here’s how the iPhone Duo compares to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8
devices.description: CNET has a series of pieces comparing the iPhone Duo to three current Android foldables. While it’s a little frustrating to tackle the comparisons separately, it seems clear that the site views Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 as the device the Duo needs to beat. That’s in large part because the two devices share similar passport-style aspect ratios rather than the tall and thin design of other foldables, and are priced only $100 apart … more…

devices.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has suggested Apple will release an "iPhone Duo Max" in the coming years, highlighting why Apple chose the "Duo" moniker over other names. devices.title: Apple's Rumored iPhone Game Controllers Will 'Likely' Come From Beats
devices.description: Earlier this month, references to two unreleased Apple game controllers were allegedly spotted in macOS 26.7 beta code, and now Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has shared more details. Power On newsletter today, Gurman said the controllers have been in development for more than a year, are for the iPhone, and will likely have Beats branding. Acquired by Apple in 2014, Beats has expanded beyond headphones and now sells charging cables, iPhone cases, and more. Related Roundup: macOS Golden Gate Tags: Beat

devices.title: iPod Touch Released 19 Years Ago Today
devices.description: The first iPod touch went on general sale on September 14, 2007, nine days after Steve Jobs unveiled it at Apple's "The Beat Goes On" media event. The device brought the iPhone's multi-touch interface, Wi-Fi, and Safari browser to the iPod lineup for the first time, but it lacked cellular phone functionality and a camera.
